    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/gmail",
    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"thread-marcus-20270428-01\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"marcus_lin\",\n  \"subject\": \"Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"marcus_lin\",\n    \"marissa_cole\",\n    \"monica_patel\",\n    \"karthik_iyer\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>\",\n    \"OliveHealth Platform <platform@olivehealth.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"4\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2027-04-28T15:20:00-07:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2027-04-30T09:14:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"sales\",\n  \"related_account\": \"OliveHealth\",\n  \"deal_id\": \"OLV-2027-073\",\n  \"region\": \"us\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"olive-traffic-sample.json\",\n    \"redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx\",\n    \"SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-olive-traces\",\n    \"HS-00045823\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai\\nDate: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700\\nSubject: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nThanks for the demo time today, Samir \\u2014 good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a short set of clarifying questions so we can size the dedicated path versus Hosted / Private VPC options: \\n\\nSummary (from today's demo)\\n- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + anonymized retrieval (low input PII, PHI-stored downstream)\\n- Latency target: interactive (sub-second p95 where possible) for the most-frequent endpoints\\n- Compliance: production data needs to be in a customer-managed VPC; non-prod can be Hosted\\n\\nClarifying questions (short answers appreciated):\\n1) Peak TPS (sustained) and short burst TPS we should plan for? (e.g., 75 TPS sustained, 200 TPS burst)\\n2) Avg/median request token mix: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, and percent that are long (>1024 tokens)\\n3) Concurrency semantics: do you need 1:1 sessions pinned, or best-effort concurrency (we optimize with batching/KV)?\\n4) P95 latency SLO for the endpoints that will be on Dedicated vs acceptable tail for Hosted fallback\\n5) Any hard requirements for KMS/BYOK, audit log retention, or region constraints beyond \\\"US\\\"?\\n\\nAttached a short sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) \\u2014 if you can drop in the traffic trace (olive-traffic-sample.json) or numbers above, we can run a quick capacity estimate and propose GPU SKU mixes (cost-first and latency-first options).\\n\\nSuggested next steps:\\n- You fill the worksheet or reply with the answers above\\n- We'll run a short projection and propose 2 SKU mixes (latency-optimized, cost-optimized) + an ops checklist for VPC onboarding\\n- If suitable, schedule a 1-hour sizing workshop next week with Ops/Infra folks\\n\\nThanks \\u2014 looping in Marissa for workshop coordination and Monica for security/compliance follow-ups.\\n\\n\\u2014 Marcus\\nMarcus Lin\\nSenior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference\\nmarcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123\\n\\nAttachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (worksheet), olive-traffic-sample.json (sample trace)\\n\",\n    \"From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>\\nTo: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai\\nCc: platform@olivehealth.com\\nDate: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:45:32 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nThanks Marcus \\u2014 appreciate the clear recap. Below are the answers (we scoped this with the infra team this morning):\\n\\n1) Traffic profile\\n- Typical daytime sustained TPS: 18 TPS across all endpoints\\n- Peak sustained TPS (end-of-month reports / campaigns): ~75 TPS sustained for 2\\u20136 hour windows\\n- Short bursts (marketing / batch jobs): up to 220 TPS for a few minutes occasionally\\n\\n2) Token mix (approx)\\n- Avg prompt tokens: 120\\n- Avg completion tokens: 250\\n- ~8% of requests exceed 1,024 tokens (mainly long summary jobs)\\n\\n3) Concurrency\\n- We expect ~20 simultaneous interactive sessions for clinical staff during peak; background jobs can be batched. We are fine with best-effort concurrency as long as p95 latency stays within SLOs for interactive endpoints.\\n\\n4) Latency SLOs\\n- Interactive endpoints: p95 <= 300ms preferred (hard requirement: <=500ms)\\n- Background summarization: p95 <= 2s is acceptable\\n\\n5) Compliance / security\\n- Production must run in our VPC (customer-managed) with KMS BYOK for encryption at rest; non-prod can be hosted.\\n- SOC2 required; attaching a pointer to our security intake (SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf) and the platform team's contact (platform@olivehealth.com).\\n\\nTimeline: aim to move to an initial Dedicated pilot in 6\\u20138 weeks if the sizing checks out.\\n\\nI uploaded a week of representative traces to the drive link you gave (folder: 1a2b3c-olive-traces). Let me know if you need raw logs or anonymized request bodies.\\n\\n\\u2014 Samir\\nSamir Khan\\nHead of Platform Engineering, OliveHealth\\nsamir.khan@olivehealth.com\\n\\nAttachments: SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf\\n\",\n    \"From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica.patel@redwood.ai\\nDate: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:10:04 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nGreat dataset \\u2014 thanks Samir, this is exactly what we need. Quick read and our initial take + proposed plan: \\n\\nInitial sizing thoughts (high level)\\n- Given the 75 TPS peak + 220 TPS short bursts and your p95 <= 300ms target for interactive endpoints, we recommend starting with a Dedicated pool that emphasizes latency with an ops-safe fallback to Hosted variants for non-critical traffic.\\n- Two SKU mixes we'll model: \\n  A) Latency-optimized: 4 x A100-80GB inference nodes (low-latency kernels, larger KV cache). This favors lower p95 at higher cost.\\n  B) Cost-optimized: 12 x A10G-style inference nodes with aggressive batching and prefix caching to hit sustained 75 TPS at lower cost, with occasional burst scaling to handle short spikes.\\n\\nNotes on architecture and tradeoffs\\n- KV/prefix caching will reduce token compute on repeated contexts (clinical templates) \\u2014 this benefits A10G options more for cost savings.\\n- Heavy long-tail requests (>1k tokens) will push memory needs; the A100-80GB config gives headroom for those workloads without model splits.\\n- For your BYOK/KMS requirement and VPC onboarding: our Private deployment (VPC/private control plane) supports customer-managed keys and audit log forwarding; Monica will follow up with the security checklist for the procurement team.\\n\\nImmediate next steps (proposed)\\n1) Marcus + I run the sizing worksheet you filled and convert traces to token-level projections (we'll do that today).\\n2) Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop next Tue or Wed with your infra + security (we're flexible) \\u2014 proposed slots: Tue May 4 10:00\\u201311:00 PT or Wed May 5 13:00\\u201314:00 PT.\\n3) If the team is comfortable with the projection, we'll spin a short Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) with monitoring hooks and rollback to Hosted for non-prod traffic.\\n\\nAction items: Samir \\u2014 confirm which workshop slot works and attach the worksheet populated if convenient. Monica \\u2014 I flagged security checklist and BYOK runbook (see related Drive link).\\n\\nThanks \\u2014 happy to jump on a call to walk through the two SKU mixes once Marcus has the projection ready.\\n\\n\\u2014 Marissa\\nMarissa Cole\\nEnterprise AE, Redwood Inference\\nmarissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199\\n\\nAttachments referenced: proposed-ops-runbook.md (link in Drive)\\n\",\n    \"From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>\\nDate: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nQuick note from infra: sounds good to me \\u2014 if you confirm the sample traces are representative we'll prioritize a capacity projection and a short benchmark (we'll exercise both SKU mixes under a synthetic traffic profile).\\n\\nKarthik\\nKarthik Iyer\\nDirector, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference\\n\",\n    \"-- End of thread --\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_fdee41e863584916a9b01d851203a0d2\"\n}",

{
  "thread_id": "thread-marcus-20270428-01",
  "mailbox_owner": "marcus_lin",
  "subject": "Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications",
  "participants_internal": [
    "marcus_lin",
    "marissa_cole",
    "monica_patel",
    "karthik_iyer"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>",
    "OliveHealth Platform <platform@olivehealth.com>"
  ],
  "message_count": "4",
  "first_email_at": "2027-04-28T15:20:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2027-04-30T09:14:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "sales",
  "related_account": "OliveHealth",
  "deal_id": "OLV-2027-073",
  "region": "us",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "olive-traffic-sample.json",
    "redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx",
    "SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-olive-traces",
    "HS-00045823"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Thanks for the demo time today, Samir — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a short set of clarifying questions so we can size the dedicated path versus Hosted / Private VPC options: 

Summary (from today's demo)
- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + anonymized retrieval (low input PII, PHI-stored downstream)
- Latency target: interactive (sub-second p95 where possible) for the most-frequent endpoints
- Compliance: production data needs to be in a customer-managed VPC; non-prod can be Hosted

Clarifying questions (short answers appreciated):
1) Peak TPS (sustained) and short burst TPS we should plan for? (e.g., 75 TPS sustained, 200 TPS burst)
2) Avg/median request token mix: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, and percent that are long (>1024 tokens)
3) Concurrency semantics: do you need 1:1 sessions pinned, or best-effort concurrency (we optimize with batching/KV)?
4) P95 latency SLO for the endpoints that will be on Dedicated vs acceptable tail for Hosted fallback
5) Any hard requirements for KMS/BYOK, audit log retention, or region constraints beyond "US"?

Attached a short sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — if you can drop in the traffic trace (olive-traffic-sample.json) or numbers above, we can run a quick capacity estimate and propose GPU SKU mixes (cost-first and latency-first options).

Suggested next steps:
- You fill the worksheet or reply with the answers above
- We'll run a short projection and propose 2 SKU mixes (latency-optimized, cost-optimized) + an ops checklist for VPC onboarding
- If suitable, schedule a 1-hour sizing workshop next week with Ops/Infra folks

Thanks — looping in Marissa for workshop coordination and Monica for security/compliance follow-ups.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (worksheet), olive-traffic-sample.json (sample trace)
",
    "From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@olivehealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:45:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. Below are the answers (we scoped this with the infra team this morning):

1) Traffic profile
- Typical daytime sustained TPS: 18 TPS across all endpoints
- Peak sustained TPS (end-of-month reports / campaigns): ~75 TPS sustained for 2–6 hour windows
- Short bursts (marketing / batch jobs): up to 220 TPS for a few minutes occasionally

2) Token mix (approx)
- Avg prompt tokens: 120
- Avg completion tokens: 250
- ~8% of requests exceed 1,024 tokens (mainly long summary jobs)

3) Concurrency
- We expect ~20 simultaneous interactive sessions for clinical staff during peak; background jobs can be batched. We are fine with best-effort concurrency as long as p95 latency stays within SLOs for interactive endpoints.

4) Latency SLOs
- Interactive endpoints: p95 <= 300ms preferred (hard requirement: <=500ms)
- Background summarization: p95 <= 2s is acceptable

5) Compliance / security
- Production must run in our VPC (customer-managed) with KMS BYOK for encryption at rest; non-prod can be hosted.
- SOC2 required; attaching a pointer to our security intake (SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf) and the platform team's contact (platform@olivehealth.com).

Timeline: aim to move to an initial Dedicated pilot in 6–8 weeks if the sizing checks out.

I uploaded a week of representative traces to the drive link you gave (folder: 1a2b3c-olive-traces). Let me know if you need raw logs or anonymized request bodies.

— Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, OliveHealth
samir.khan@olivehealth.com

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf
",
    "From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:10:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Great dataset — thanks Samir, this is exactly what we need. Quick read and our initial take + proposed plan: 

Initial sizing thoughts (high level)
- Given the 75 TPS peak + 220 TPS short bursts and your p95 <= 300ms target for interactive endpoints, we recommend starting with a Dedicated pool that emphasizes latency with an ops-safe fallback to Hosted variants for non-critical traffic.
- Two SKU mixes we'll model: 
  A) Latency-optimized: 4 x A100-80GB inference nodes (low-latency kernels, larger KV cache). This favors lower p95 at higher cost.
  B) Cost-optimized: 12 x A10G-style inference nodes with aggressive batching and prefix caching to hit sustained 75 TPS at lower cost, with occasional burst scaling to handle short spikes.

Notes on architecture and tradeoffs
- KV/prefix caching will reduce token compute on repeated contexts (clinical templates) — this benefits A10G options more for cost savings.
- Heavy long-tail requests (>1k tokens) will push memory needs; the A100-80GB config gives headroom for those workloads without model splits.
- For your BYOK/KMS requirement and VPC onboarding: our Private deployment (VPC/private control plane) supports customer-managed keys and audit log forwarding; Monica will follow up with the security checklist for the procurement team.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Marcus + I run the sizing worksheet you filled and convert traces to token-level projections (we'll do that today).
2) Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop next Tue or Wed with your infra + security (we're flexible) — proposed slots: Tue May 4 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed May 5 13:00–14:00 PT.
3) If the team is comfortable with the projection, we'll spin a short Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) with monitoring hooks and rollback to Hosted for non-prod traffic.

Action items: Samir — confirm which workshop slot works and attach the worksheet populated if convenient. Monica — I flagged security checklist and BYOK runbook (see related Drive link).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the two SKU mixes once Marcus has the projection ready.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments referenced: proposed-ops-runbook.md (link in Drive)
",
    "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Quick note from infra: sounds good to me — if you confirm the sample traces are representative we'll prioritize a capacity projection and a short benchmark (we'll exercise both SKU mixes under a synthetic traffic profile).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
",

{
  "thread_id": "thread_20260310_laura_hc_001",
  "mailbox_owner": "Laura Bennett",
  "subject": "Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze",
  "participants_internal": [
    "Laura Bennett",
    "Vivek Kulkarni",
    "Evelyn Hart",
    "Markus Klein",
    "Priya Natarajan"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "recruiting@peoplelogic.com",
    "Greenhouse (no-reply@greenhouse.io)"
  ],
  "message_count": "5",
  "first_email_at": "2026-03-10T09:15:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-03-12T14:22:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "leadership_update",
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExAMPLE/headcount-q2",
    "HUBSPOT-12458"
  ],
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "headcount_request_Q2_v2.xlsx",
    "req_summary_Q2.pdf"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Team —

As we finalize Q2 plans in next week's leadership sync and QBR prep, we need a quick (48h) alignment on headcount priorities and any outstanding req approvals. Key asks:

- Evelyn: can you attach the latest req spreadsheet and indicate which reqs are already HR-approved vs pending finance/headcount?
- Markus: what is the threshold for triggering a temporary hiring freeze this quarter given current spend vs plan?
- Vivek & Priya: highlight top 3 hires you consider mission-critical (backfills or net-new) and why they can't be delayed to Q3.

Context: execs are evaluating a modest contingency scenario if cloud costs stay above forecast. We want to avoid surprises in the QBR. Attached is my consolidated version of requests (headcount_request_Q2_v2.xlsx).

Please reply with short bullets (2–3 lines each). I will summarize for Friday's leadership packet.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People & Org Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: headcount_request_Q2_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
",
    "From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Laura —

Quick bullets:

1) Mission-critical (top 3):
   - Senior Inference Engineer (backfill for Aditya Rao): required for ongoing runtime optimizations tied to a customer SLA; delaying risks churn on two pilot accounts.
   - MLP Backend Engineer (net-new, infra team): enables autoscaling improvements to reduce per-token costs; high ROI within 6–8 weeks.
   - Senior SRE (backfill): we are 30% under-target for on-call coverage; hiring lag is adding operational risk.

2) Flex candidates: Mid-level SWE roles can be deprioritized or converted to contractors for Q2.

3) If we need to pause, freeze should apply to net-new IC headcount first; backfills for critical SLAs should be exempted with approval from both you and Markus.

I'll flag specific req IDs in the spreadsheet.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Engineering

On Tue, Mar 10, 2026 at 09:15 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> As we finalize Q2 plans...
",
    "From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Laura / all —

Short finance view:

- Current run-rate vs plan: we're tracking ~6% above the cash flow assumption due to higher cloud spend and a couple of late professional services invoices.
- Hiring freeze trigger: If we cannot get run-rate back to plan within 6 weeks with cost mitigations, we should impose a temporary freeze on net-new roles. Backfills for critical operational roles (SRE, core infra, CS escalation owners) are allowed with written approval from Laura + my sign-off.
- Approvals: I can clear up to 4 FTEs this quarter from discretionary budget; anything beyond requires CFO/CEO approval.

Evelyn: please mark reqs that are time-sensitive and provide expected start dates; that will help prioritize the 4 discretionary slots.

-Markus
CFO (Interim)
Markus Klein

On Tue, Mar 10, 2026 at 10:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Laura —
> 
> Quick bullets:
",
    "From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Hi all —

I've updated the req tracker (attached: req_summary_Q2.pdf) and added columns: HR status, Finance status, requested start, and priority tag (Critical / High / Medium). Summary:

- HR-approved & ready to post: 5 reqs (including Vivek's Senior Inference Engineer backfill).
- Pending finance sign-off: 6 reqs (mostly net-new).
- Time-sensitive backfills (need start by 05/01 to avoid risks): 3 reqs (SRE, Inference Eng, CS Escalation Lead).

Notes / asks:
- Priya: your two reqs show as HR-approved — if you need expedited offers, loop recruiting@peoplelogic.com (cc'd).
- Markus: can you confirm which of the 6 pending finance sign-offs you'd prioritize for your discretionary 4 slots?

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Director, People Operations

Attachment: req_summary_Q2.pdf (PDF stub)

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 08:47 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Laura / all —
",
    "From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Laura / team —

Agree with Vivek and Markus on freeze semantics. Quick prioritization from my bucket:

1) Senior Product Manager (backfill for recent departure) — Critical: product roadmap for embeddings/infra depends on PM guidance; risk to partner commitments if not filled by mid-May.
2) Staff PM (net-new) — High: strategic but can push to Q3 if needed.
3) Senior UX Researcher (net-new) — Medium: nice-to-have for next-phase experiments.

If we get 2 discretionary slots from Markus, please prioritize the PM backfill + Vivek's Inference Eng backfill. Evelyn: I can fast-track candidate approvals this week. Recruiting is copied.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Head of Product, Inference

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 12:05 PM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi all —

    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json",
    "title": "ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\",\n  \"space\": \"architecture-and-standards\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Martinez\",\n    \"Sara Kim\",\n    \"Liam O'Connor\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"adr\",\n    \"contract-testing\",\n    \"schema-fencing\",\n    \"ci-cd\",\n    \"conformance\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\",\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n\\nThis ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary \\\"schema fencing\\\" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.\\n\\nContext and motivation\\n\\nRecent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:\\n\\n- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).\\n- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).\\n- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.\\n\\nThis ADR proposes:\\n\\n1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.\\n2. A \\\"schema fencing\\\" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.\\n3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.\\n\\nScope\\n\\nApplies to:\\n\\n- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).\\n- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).\\n- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n\\n- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.\\n- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.\\n\\nKey concepts\\n\\nDeclarative contract test spec (DCTS):\\n- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).\\n- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).\\n\\nSchema fencing:\\n- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.\\n- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.\\n\\nConformance matrix and ledger:\\n- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.\\n- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.\\n\\nRules and compatibility classes\\n\\nFields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:\\n\\n- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.\\n- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.\\n- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.\\n- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).\\n\\nChange proposal workflow (brief)\\n\\n1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.\\n2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.\\n3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.\\n4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.\\n\\nExample DCTS snippet (YAML)\\n\\n# Example: /v1/generate request/response\\n# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml\\n---\\nendpoint: POST /v1/generate\\nscope: public\\nversion: 1.0.0\\nmode: strict\\nrequest: \\n  content-type: application/json\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      prompt:\\n        type: string\\n      features:\\n        type: object\\n        additionalProperties: true\\n    required: [prompt]\\nexamples:\\n  - name: simplest\\n    request: {\\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Summarize the following text...\\\"}\\nresponse:\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      id: {type: string}\\n      output: {type: string}\\n      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}\\n    required: [id, output]\\npredicates:\\n  - description: output must be non-empty\\n    jq: \\\".output | length > 0\\\"\\nconformance_category: strict\\n\\nAutomation and CI integration\\n\\nCI responsibilities (service repo):\\n- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).\\n- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).\\n- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.\\n\\nCross-repo conformance job (central):\\n- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.\\n- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.\\n\\nConformance ledger and dashboard\\n\\nThe ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)\\n\\nRequired columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.\\n\\nOperational SLOs and alerting\\n\\n- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.\\n- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.\\n\\nGating and release policy\\n\\n- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.\\n- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.\\n\\nRollout and rollback playbook (high level)\\n\\n1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.\\n2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.\\n3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.\\n4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.\\n5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.\\n\\nTelemetry and observability requirements\\n\\nEach contract-test run must emit:\\n- conftest.run_id (UUID)\\n- conftest.service (service name/version)\\n- conftest.endpoint\\n- conftest.test_case_id\\n- conftest.result (pass|fail)\\n- conftest.duration_ms\\n\\nThese fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.\\n\\nOwner and stewardship\\n\\n- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.\\n- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.\\n\\nOpen questions and tradeoffs\\n\\n- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.\\n- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).\\n\\nMigration plan\\n\\n1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.\\n2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.\\n3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.\\n\\nAppendix: sample CLI commands and linter config\\n\\n# Local validation\\n#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml\\n\\n# Publish artifact (CI step)\\n#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml\\n\\n# Central conformance run (dry-run example)\\n#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv\\n\\n# Linter rules (excerpt)\\n# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]\\n\\nNotes on documentation style\\n\\n- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.\\n- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.\\n\\nReferences\\n\\n- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\\n- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\\n\\nApproval\\n\\nApproved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_04b24bf957c047f4b7d8ceefdfde8290\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\nnew field marked extension : always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields ( tolerant mode ). change proposal workflow ( brief ) 1. author creates a cp file in the service repo under docs / contracts / cps / < pr >. yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria. 2. ci runs : unit tests, dcts local run, contract linters, and cross - service dry - run against the latest conformance snapshot. 3. if auto - check passes ( non - breaking or safe extension ), merge proceeds. if flagged as potentially breaking, the cp moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners. 4. after merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.",

{
  "title": "ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing",
  "space": "architecture-and-standards",
  "author": "Aisha Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-03-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Martinez",
    "Sara Kim",
    "Liam O'Connor"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "adr",
    "contract-testing",
    "schema-fencing",
    "ci-cd",
    "conformance"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025",
    "/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Summary

This ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary "schema fencing" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.

Context and motivation

Recent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:

- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).
- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).
- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.

This ADR proposes:

1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.
2. A "schema fencing" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.
3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.

Scope

Applies to:

- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).
- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).
- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.

Out of scope:

- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.
- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.

Key concepts

Declarative contract test spec (DCTS):
- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).
- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).

Schema fencing:
- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.
- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.

Conformance matrix and ledger:
- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.
- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.

Rules and compatibility classes

Fields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:

- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.
- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.
- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.
- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).

Change proposal workflow (brief)

1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.
2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.
3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.
4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.

Example DCTS snippet (YAML)

# Example: /v1/generate request/response
# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml
---
endpoint: POST /v1/generate
scope: public
version: 1.0.0
mode: strict
request: 
  content-type: application/json
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      prompt:
        type: string
      features:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: true
    required: [prompt]
examples:
  - name: simplest
    request: {"prompt": "Summarize the following text..."}
response:
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      id: {type: string}
      output: {type: string}
      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}
    required: [id, output]
predicates:
  - description: output must be non-empty
    jq: ".output | length > 0"
conformance_category: strict

Automation and CI integration

CI responsibilities (service repo):
- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).
- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).
- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.

Cross-repo conformance job (central):
- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.
- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.

Conformance ledger and dashboard

The ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)

Required columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.

Operational SLOs and alerting

- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.
- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.

Gating and release policy

- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.
- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.

Rollout and rollback playbook (high level)

1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.
2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.
3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.
4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.
5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.

Telemetry and observability requirements

Each contract-test run must emit:
- conftest.run_id (UUID)
- conftest.service (service name/version)
- conftest.endpoint
- conftest.test_case_id
- conftest.result (pass|fail)
- conftest.duration_ms

These fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.

Owner and stewardship

- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.
- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.

Open questions and tradeoffs

- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.
- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).

Migration plan

1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.
2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.
3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.

Appendix: sample CLI commands and linter config

# Local validation
#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml

# Publish artifact (CI step)
#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml

# Central conformance run (dry-run example)
#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv

# Linter rules (excerpt)
# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]

Notes on documentation style

- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.
- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.

References

- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025
- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026

Approval

Approved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.

Agreed on next steps: a take-home assignment and scheduling a panel interview.\",\n  \"topics\": [\n    \"background and experience\",\n    \"technical troubleshooting scenario\",\n    \"Redwood product fit\",\n    \"next steps and scheduling\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Sophie to send take-home assignment by 2025-02-12\",\n    \"Schedule panel interview with PM and Eng by 2025-02-18\",\n    \"Recruiter to confirm candidate availability\"\n  ],\n  \"action_items\": [\n    \"Sophie Martinez - send assignment - 2025-02-12\",\n    \"Evan Liu - prepare technical rubric and notes - 2025-02-14\",\n    \"Leah Kim - confirm panel availability - 2025-02-13\"\n  ],\n  \"competitors_mentioned\": [\n    \"Databricks\",\n    \"Anthropic\"\n  ],\n  \"transcript\": \"Meeting Header:\\nDate: 2025-02-11\\nTime: 16:00 PST\\nDuration: 40 minutes\\nAttendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Candidate), Leah Kim (Recruiter)\\n\\n[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sophie from Redwood, Evan's with me. Priya, thanks for taking the time today. Can you hear us ok?\\n[00:08] Priya Rao: Yes, I can hear you. Thanks for having me.\\n[00:12] Evan Liu: Great, we'll start with a quick intro then jump to a short technical scenario. Sounds good?\\n[00:16] Priya Rao: Sounds perfect.\\n[00:20] Sophie Martinez: Cool. Priya, can you give a 2-3 minute background\\u2014recent roles, what you've been shipping, and why you're interested in Redwood?\\n[00:32] Priya Rao: Sure. I most recently was at InfraAnalytics where I was a senior solutions engineer supporting AI infra customers, mostly focused on model serving and cost optimizations. I worked a lot with GPU provisioning, autoscaling policies, and helping customers design fallback routing for multi-model setups. I'm excited about Redwood because of the focus on production-grade inference\\u2014I've seen a lot of customers struggle with predictable latency and cost, so the product fit seems good for my background.\\n[01:05] Evan Liu: When you say autoscaling policies, can you give an example\\u2014like what metrics you tuned and tradeoffs you considered?\\n[01:12] Priya Rao: We tuned on queue length and P95 latency for the endpoint. The tradeoff was throughput vs. cold-starts; we had to pick batch windows carefully so spikes didn't blow up latency, and we used a small warm pool to avoid tail latency for critical routes. Also we used quantized weights at night for cost savings on non-critical workloads.\\n[01:38] Sophie Martinez: Nice, that aligns with what our Optimize team talks about. Quick question about customer conversations\\u2014how did you surface reliability concerns without scaring customers about cost?\\n[01:50] Priya Rao: I led with SLOs and a simple example: show them current costs and what latency looks like with and without aggressive batching. I often propose a two-stage rollout: first optimize for cost in staging, then pin to a more conservative config in prod and monitor.\\n[02:10] Evan Liu: Ok, let's do a short troubleshooting scenario. Imagine a customer reports intermittent 5xxs from streaming API when traffic spikes. Walk me through your investigation and immediate mitigations.\\n[02:22] Priya Rao: First I'd confirm the scope: is it a single model, region, or route? Check the gateway and per-route logs, look at KV cache hit rates, and check GPU memory pressure. Immediate mitigations: enable rate-limiting/queue throttling, fallback to a lower-capacity model variant, or divert non-critical traffic to a cached response. For long-term fix, tune batching thresholds and increase warm pool or adjust autoscaler cooldowns.\\n[03:05] Evan Liu: In practice, when you say divert to cached response, what kind of cache policies did you use?\\n[03:12] Priya Rao: Mostly prefix and user-session cache for deterministic flows, TTL-based for semistochastic outputs. We were careful with PII\\u2014consistent with KMS policies\\u2014so cache keys were hashed and encrypted.\\n[03:30] Sophie Martinez: There's sometimes confusion between caching and reranking\\u2014good answer. Follow-up: have you ever helped design a private deployment or VPC/on-prem setup?\\n[03:40] Priya Rao: Yes, we ran a couple private deployments. Main issues were networking: TLS cert management, DNS, and ensuring audit logs to the customer's SIEM. For onboarding we provided runbooks for firewall rules and IAM roles.\\n[03:58] Evan Liu: Any experience with HSM/KMS integrations?\\n[04:02] Priya Rao: Yes, customers usually had a preferred KMS. We wrote examples for AWS KMS and a generic HSM handshake.\\n[04:12] Leah Kim: Priya, quick note on timeline\\u2014are you available for a take-home exercise this week?\\n[04:18] Priya Rao: Yes, I am. I can take it and return within 48 hours.\\n[04:22] Sophie Martinez: Great. Final part: do you have any questions for us?\\n[04:26] Priya Rao: A couple. One, how do teams at Redwood balance latency SLOs vs. model cost when running mixed workloads? Two, what's the typical ramp for a new hire in SE?\\n[04:36] Evan Liu: For the first\\u2014it's a combination of RBAC-based routing and workload tagging; we use profiling to recommend quantization, autoscale settings, and sometimes model-variant routing. In product it's a lot of labelling routes by criticality and setting different batch windows.\\n[04:52] Sophie Martinez: On ramp\\u2014two weeks onboarding then shadowing calls for about a month; you pair with an AE/SE for the first quarter on new accounts.\\n[05:00] Priya Rao: That sounds good.\\n[05:03] Sophie Martinez: Ok we'll wrap. Leah, we'll send the take-home and schedule the panel. Priya, thanks again.\\n[05:10] Leah Kim: Thanks, everyone.\\n\\n(Transcription notes: occasional overlap and filler words; some technical terms auto-corrected\\u2014e.g., KV cache was sometimes transcribed as \\\"K-V cash\\\").\",\n  \"dataset_noise_document\": true,\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"summary\",\n    \"transcript\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_2c9dcc3afa3249f39c725884e5be5c72\"\n}",

{
  "meeting_id": "ff-20250211-001",
  "recorded_at": "2025-02-11T16:00:00-08:00",
  "duration_minutes": "40",
  "call_type": "other",
  "title": "Candidate Interview: Senior Sales Engineer",
  "redwood_owner": "Sophie Martinez",
  "redwood_attendees": [
    "Sophie Martinez",
    "Evan Liu"
  ],
  "customer_company": "Candidate: Priya Rao",
  "customer_attendees": [
    "Priya Rao (Candidate)",
    "Leah Kim (Recruiter)"
  ],
  "transcription_quality": "medium",
  "summary": "First-stage technical interview for a Senior Sales Engineer candidate. Covered candidate background, systems experience, brief product walkthrough, and a short troubleshooting scenario. Agreed on next steps: a take-home assignment and scheduling a panel interview.",
  "topics": [
    "background and experience",
    "technical troubleshooting scenario",
    "Redwood product fit",
    "next steps and scheduling"
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Sophie to send take-home assignment by 2025-02-12",
    "Schedule panel interview with PM and Eng by 2025-02-18",
    "Recruiter to confirm candidate availability"
  ],
  "action_items": [
    "Sophie Martinez - send assignment - 2025-02-12",
    "Evan Liu - prepare technical rubric and notes - 2025-02-14",
    "Leah Kim - confirm panel availability - 2025-02-13"
  ],
  "competitors_mentioned": [
    "Databricks",
    "Anthropic"
  ],
  "transcript": "Meeting Header:\nDate: 2025-02-11\nTime: 16:00 PST\nDuration: 40 minutes\nAttendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Candidate), Leah Kim (Recruiter)\n\n[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sophie from Redwood, Evan's with me. Priya, thanks for taking the time today. Can you hear us ok?\n[00:08] Priya Rao: Yes, I can hear you. Thanks for having me.\n[00:12] Evan Liu: Great, we'll start with a quick intro then jump to a short technical scenario. Sounds good?\n[00:16] Priya Rao: Sounds perfect.\n[00:20] Sophie Martinez: Cool. Priya, can you give a 2-3 minute background\u2014recent roles, what you've been shipping, and why you're interested in Redwood?\n[00:32] Priya Rao: Sure. I most recently was at InfraAnalytics where I was a senior solutions engineer supporting AI infra customers, mostly focused on model serving and cost optimizations. I worked a lot with GPU provisioning, autoscaling policies, and helping customers design fallback routing for multi-model setups. I'm excited about Redwood because of the focus on production-grade inference\u2014I've seen a lot of customers struggle with predictable latency and cost, so the product fit seems good for my background.\n[01:05] Evan Liu: When you say autoscaling policies, can you give an example\u2014like what metrics you tuned and tradeoffs you considered?\n[01:12] Priya Rao: We tuned on queue length and P95 latency for the endpoint. The tradeoff was throughput vs. cold-starts; we had to pick batch windows carefully so spikes didn't blow up latency, and we used a small warm pool to avoid tail latency for critical routes. Also we used quantized weights at night for cost savings on non-critical workloads.\n[01:38] Sophie Martinez: Nice, that aligns with what our Optimize team talks about. Quick question about customer conversations\u2014how did you surface reliability concerns without scaring customers about cost?\n[01:50] Priya Rao: I led with SLOs and a simple example: show them current costs and what latency looks like with and without aggressive batching. I often propose a two-stage rollout: first optimize for cost in staging, then pin to a more conservative config in prod and monitor.\n[02:10] Evan Liu: Ok, let's do a short troubleshooting scenario. Imagine a customer reports intermittent 5xxs from streaming API when traffic spikes. Walk me through your investigation and immediate mitigations.\n[02:22] Priya Rao: First I'd confirm the scope: is it a single model, region, or route? Check the gateway and per-route logs, look at KV cache hit rates, and check GPU memory pressure. Immediate mitigations: enable rate-limiting/queue throttling, fallback to a lower-capacity model variant, or divert non-critical traffic to a cached response. For long-term fix, tune batching thresholds and increase warm pool or adjust autoscaler cooldowns.\n[03:05] Evan Liu: In practice, when you say divert to cached response, what kind of cache policies did you use?\n[03:12] Priya Rao: Mostly prefix and user-session cache for deterministic flows, TTL-based for semistochastic outputs. We were careful with PII\u2014consistent with KMS policies\u2014so cache keys were hashed and encrypted.\n[03:30] Sophie Martinez: There's sometimes confusion between caching and reranking\u2014good answer. Follow-up: have you ever helped design a private deployment or VPC/on-prem setup?\n[03:40] Priya Rao: Yes, we ran a couple private deployments. Main issues were networking: TLS cert management, DNS, and ensuring audit logs to the customer's SIEM. For onboarding we provided runbooks for firewall rules and IAM roles.\n[03:58] Evan Liu: Any experience with HSM/KMS integrations?\n[04:02] Priya Rao: Yes, customers usually had a preferred KMS. We wrote examples for AWS KMS and a generic HSM handshake.\n[04:12] Leah Kim: Priya, quick note on timeline\u2014are you available for a take-home exercise this week?\n[04:18] Priya Rao: Yes, I am. I can take it and return within 48 hours.\n[04:22] Sophie Martinez: Great. Final part: do you have any questions for us?\n[04:26] Priya Rao: A couple. One, how do teams at Redwood balance latency SLOs vs. model cost when running mixed workloads? Two, what's the typical ramp for a new hire in SE?\n[04:36] Evan Liu: For the first\u2014it's a combination of RBAC-based routing and workload tagging; we use profiling to recommend quantization, autoscale settings, and sometimes model-variant routing. In product it's a lot of labelling routes by criticality and setting different batch windows.\n[04:52] Sophie Martinez: On ramp\u2014two weeks onboarding then shadowing calls for about a month; you pair with an AE/SE for the first quarter on new accounts.\n[05:00] Priya Rao: That sounds good.\n[05:03] Sophie Martinez: Ok we'll wrap. Leah, we'll send the take-home and schedule the panel. Priya, thanks again.\n[05:10] Leah Kim: Thanks, everyone.\n\n(Transcription notes: occasional overlap and filler words; some technical terms auto-corrected\u2014e.g., KV cache was sometimes transcribed as \"K-V cash\").",

  "content_field_names": [

    "transcript"

    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"95312\",\n  \"title\": \"Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)\",\n  \"author\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-18\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-24\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-02-24\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/sdk-cross-handshake-consumer-ergonomics\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Raj Patel\",\n    \"Elena Kuznetsova\",\n    \"Samir Nair\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"sdk\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"auth\",\n    \"perf\",\n    \"chore\",\n    \"release-notes\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-2142\",\n    \"ENG-2178\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_jira\": [\n    \"SUP-312\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"11\",\n  \"additions\": \"642\",\n  \"deletions\": \"211\",\n  \"description\": \"Motivation: We have diverging streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs and subtle auth-retry edge cases that manifest as half-open streams or token race conditions during refresh. This PR unifies three areas: 1) a minimal, consistent 3-way auth handshake for stream starts and reconnects; 2) a small, opinionated consumer surface that makes backpressure and heartbeats explicit but ergonomic; 3) a single, test-backed retry policy and token-refresh hook that avoids duplicate requests during auth rotation.\\n\\nSummary of changes (high level):\\n- Introduce a lightweight stream handshake: CLIENT_HELLO -> AUTH_OK -> SERVER_READY. Implemented in each SDK with shared semantics and compatibility fallbacks for older servers.\\n- Consumer ergonomics: new thin abstraction that replaces ad-hoc iterators/callbacks. Python exposes StreamConsumer (AsyncIterator + context manager) with buffer_size and heartbeat_ack semantics; TS exposes createStreamConsumer({onMessage, onComplete, bufferSize}) and an async iterable wrapper; Go exposes StreamReader(ctx) that implements io.Reader-like semantics for single-message reads and a Cancel() helper.\\n- Auth/retries: unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy across SDKs. Retries are jittered exponential with token refresh hook invoked once per logical request; transparent idempotency guard added for non-idempotent unary calls.\\n- Backwards compatibility: consumers detect old handshake flows and fall back to legacy behavior for servers that do not return AUTH_OK. Migration warnings are surfaced at runtime (single warn log per process).\\n- Tests: added unit tests for handshake transitions and integration e2e stream tests in a local harness that simulates mid-stream token expiration.\\n- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.\\n\\nWhy this shape: the platform-level serving runtime already relies on explicit stream lifecycle events; exposing a small, consistent surface across SDKs reduces footguns (double-sends during reauth, leaked goroutines or pending async generators) and improves observability for consumers.\\n\\nMigration notes:\\n- Python: replace raw async for msg in client.stream() with: async with client.stream_consumer() as c: async for msg in c: ...; short-lived code paths still supported but deprecated.\\n- TS: prefer createStreamConsumer over stream().iterator() when you need backpressure controls.\\n- Go: use NewStreamReader(ctx) to ensure reads cancel cleanly on token refresh.\\n\\nChecklist: \\n- [x] Cross-SDK API proposals agreed with SDK leads (Raj/Elena)\\n- [x] Unit + integration tests added\\n- [x] CI flake triaged and rerun (see CI summary)\\n- [x] Changelog & migration guide updated\\n\\nNotes: this PR intentionally keeps signal surface minimal (3 flags + 2 callbacks) to avoid burdening consumers. See linked Linear ENG-2142 for design doc.\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"a1f3b9d: sdk: add handshake primitives and shared test harness\",\n    \"b4e2c10: python: StreamConsumer implementation, tests and deprecation warnings\",\n    \"c7d9f21: typescript: createStreamConsumer, iterable adapter and examples\",\n    \"d2a7eba: go: NewStreamReader + cancel semantics and integration test\",\n    \"f1b5c30: common: retry-with-auth-refresh policy and idempotency guard\",\n    \"e3c8f5a: docs: migration guide and changelogs for python/ts/go\"\n  ],\n  \"files_changed\": [\n    \"redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streaming/consumer.py\",\n    \"redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_stream_handshake.py\",\n    \"redwood-sdk-typescript/src/stream/consumer.ts\",\n    \"redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/streaming-backpressure.md\",\n    \"redwood-sdk-go/stream/reader.go\",\n    \"redwood-sdk-go/stream/read_test.go\",\n    \"shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy.go\",\n    \"shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy_test.go\",\n    \"docs/migration/streaming-migration.md\",\n    \"CHANGELOGs/SDKs.md\",\n    \"tools/test-harness/stream-proxy-sim.js\"\n  ],\n  \"review_comments\": [\n    \"Raj: Can we avoid a second token refresh race if two concurrent streams call the hook? Suggest ensuring the hook is single-flight per token_id. Response: implemented singleflight guard in shared retry_policy with metrics (auth_refresh_locks).\",\n    \"Elena: TS consumer ergonomics look good but question on buffer default. Response: default buffer_size changed to 16 and documented rationale (latency vs memory).\",\n    \"Samir: Go Cancel() semantics \\u2014 will it leak goroutines when Cancel is called mid-read? Response: added explicit test and closed goroutine via consistent context cancellation path; verified in go race run.\",\n    \"CI-bot: e2e streaming failed when simulating token expiry. Author: added extra wait/retry in harness and hardened backoff; reran and passed.\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"unit (python/ts/go): pass\",\n    \"lint (python/ts/go): pass\",\n    \"integration (stream e2e harness): initial fail (token race) -> fix -> pass\",\n    \"e2e (smoke): pass\",\n    \"security-scan: pass\"\n  ],\n  \"merge_method\": \"squash\",\n  \"merge_outcome\": \"merged\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"- SDKs: unify streaming handshake semantics across Python/TS/Go; introduce ergonomic StreamConsumer/StreamReader abstractions.\\n- Auth: single-flight token refresh hook and unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy to avoid duplicate in-flight retries.\\n- Backwards compatibility: servers without AUTH_OK are supported with harmless warnings.\\n- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.\\n- Migration guidance added to docs/migration/streaming-migration.md\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"notes_for_release_manager\": \"This is a cross-SDK change: coordinate SDK package publishes in the same release window to avoid mixed-version consumer code paths. Defer rollout of deprecation warnings for 2 weeks after release.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_comments\",\n    \"release_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_88b39d13bd584ef8b1422d76994808c7\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\n\ndescription : motivation : we have diverging streaming ergonomics across python / ts / go sdks and subtle auth - retry edge cases that manifest as half - open streams or token race conditions during refresh. this pr unifies three areas : 1 ) a minimal, consistent 3 - way auth handshake for stream starts and reconnects ; 2 ) a small, opinionated consumer surface that makes backpressure and heartbeats explicit but ergonomic ; 3 ) a single, test - backed retry policy and token - refresh hook that avoids duplicate requests during auth",

document.content:
{
  "repo": "redwood",
  "pr_number": "95312",
  "title": "Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)",
  "author": "Maya Chen",
  "created_at": "2026-02-18",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-24",
  "merged_at": "2026-02-24",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/sdk-cross-handshake-consumer-ergonomics",
  "reviewers": [
    "Raj Patel",
    "Elena Kuznetsova",
    "Samir Nair"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "sdk",
    "streaming",
    "auth",
    "perf",
    "chore",
    "release-notes"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-2142",
    "ENG-2178"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "SUP-312"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "11",
  "additions": "642",
  "deletions": "211",
  "description": "Motivation: We have diverging streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs and subtle auth-retry edge cases that manifest as half-open streams or token race conditions during refresh. This PR unifies three areas: 1) a minimal, consistent 3-way auth handshake for stream starts and reconnects; 2) a small, opinionated consumer surface that makes backpressure and heartbeats explicit but ergonomic; 3) a single, test-backed retry policy and token-refresh hook that avoids duplicate requests during auth rotation.\n\nSummary of changes (high level):\n- Introduce a lightweight stream handshake: CLIENT_HELLO -> AUTH_OK -> SERVER_READY. Implemented in each SDK with shared semantics and compatibility fallbacks for older servers.\n- Consumer ergonomics: new thin abstraction that replaces ad-hoc iterators/callbacks. Python exposes StreamConsumer (AsyncIterator + context manager) with buffer_size and heartbeat_ack semantics; TS exposes createStreamConsumer({onMessage, onComplete, bufferSize}) and an async iterable wrapper; Go exposes StreamReader(ctx) that implements io.Reader-like semantics for single-message reads and a Cancel() helper.\n- Auth/retries: unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy across SDKs. Retries are jittered exponential with token refresh hook invoked once per logical request; transparent idempotency guard added for non-idempotent unary calls.\n- Backwards compatibility: consumers detect old handshake flows and fall back to legacy behavior for servers that do not return AUTH_OK. Migration warnings are surfaced at runtime (single warn log per process).\n- Tests: added unit tests for handshake transitions and integration e2e stream tests in a local harness that simulates mid-stream token expiration.\n- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.\n\nWhy this shape: the platform-level serving runtime already relies on explicit stream lifecycle events; exposing a small, consistent surface across SDKs reduces footguns (double-sends during reauth, leaked goroutines or pending async generators) and improves observability for consumers.\n\nMigration notes:\n- Python: replace raw async for msg in client.stream() with: async with client.stream_consumer() as c: async for msg in c: ...; short-lived code paths still supported but deprecated.\n- TS: prefer createStreamConsumer over stream().iterator() when you need backpressure controls.\n- Go: use NewStreamReader(ctx) to ensure reads cancel cleanly on token refresh.\n\nChecklist: \n- [x] Cross-SDK API proposals agreed with SDK leads (Raj/Elena)\n- [x] Unit + integration tests added\n- [x] CI flake triaged and rerun (see CI summary)\n- [x] Changelog & migration guide updated\n\nNotes: this PR intentionally keeps signal surface minimal (3 flags + 2 callbacks) to avoid burdening consumers. See linked Linear ENG-2142 for design doc.",
  "commits": [
    "a1f3b9d: sdk: add handshake primitives and shared test harness",
    "b4e2c10: python: StreamConsumer implementation, tests and deprecation warnings",
    "c7d9f21: typescript: createStreamConsumer, iterable adapter and examples",
    "d2a7eba: go: NewStreamReader + cancel semantics and integration test",
    "f1b5c30: common: retry-with-auth-refresh policy and idempotency guard",
    "e3c8f5a: docs: migration guide and changelogs for python/ts/go"
  ],
  "files_changed": [
    "redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streaming/consumer.py",
    "redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_stream_handshake.py",
    "redwood-sdk-typescript/src/stream/consumer.ts",
    "redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/streaming-backpressure.md",
    "redwood-sdk-go/stream/reader.go",
    "redwood-sdk-go/stream/read_test.go",
    "shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy.go",
    "shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy_test.go",
    "docs/migration/streaming-migration.md",
    "CHANGELOGs/SDKs.md",
    "tools/test-harness/stream-proxy-sim.js"
  ],
  "review_comments": [
    "Raj: Can we avoid a second token refresh race if two concurrent streams call the hook? Suggest ensuring the hook is single-flight per token_id. Response: implemented singleflight guard in shared retry_policy with metrics (auth_refresh_locks).",
    "Elena: TS consumer ergonomics look good but question on buffer default. Response: default buffer_size changed to 16 and documented rationale (latency vs memory).",
    "Samir: Go Cancel() semantics \u2014 will it leak goroutines when Cancel is called mid-read? Response: added explicit test and closed goroutine via consistent context cancellation path; verified in go race run.",
    "CI-bot: e2e streaming failed when simulating token expiry. Author: added extra wait/retry in harness and hardened backoff; reran and passed."
  ],
  "ci_checks": [
    "unit (python/ts/go): pass",
    "lint (python/ts/go): pass",
    "integration (stream e2e harness): initial fail (token race) -> fix -> pass",
    "e2e (smoke): pass",
    "security-scan: pass"
  ],
  "merge_method": "squash",
  "merge_outcome": "merged",
  "release_notes": "- SDKs: unify streaming handshake semantics across Python/TS/Go; introduce ergonomic StreamConsumer/StreamReader abstractions.\n- Auth: single-flight token refresh hook and unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy to avoid duplicate in-flight retries.\n- Backwards compatibility: servers without AUTH_OK are supported with harmless warnings.\n- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.\n- Migration guidance added to docs/migration/streaming-migration.md",
  "breaking_change": "false",
  "notes_for_release_manager": "This is a cross-SDK change: coordinate SDK package publishes in the same release window to avoid mixed-version consumer code paths. Defer rollout of deprecation warnings for 2 weeks after release.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "review_comments",
    "release_notes"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_88b39d13bd584ef8b1422d76994808c7"
}

Key asks:\\n\\n- Evelyn: can you attach the latest req spreadsheet and indicate which reqs are already HR-approved vs pending finance/headcount?\\n- Markus: what is the threshold for triggering a temporary hiring freeze this quarter given current spend vs plan?\\n- Vivek & Priya: highlight top 3 hires you consider mission-critical (backfills or net-new) and why they can't be delayed to Q3.\\n\\nContext: execs are evaluating a modest contingency scenario if cloud costs stay above forecast. We want to avoid surprises in the QBR. Attached is my consolidated version of requests (headcount_request_Q2_v2.xlsx).\\n\\nPlease reply with short bullets (2\\u20133 lines each). I will summarize for Friday's leadership packet.\\n\\nThanks \\u2014\\nLaura\\nLaura Bennett\\nVP, People & Org Strategy\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nAttachment: headcount_request_Q2_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)\\n\",\n    \"From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>\\nTo: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>\\nDate: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze\\n\\nLaura \\u2014\\n\\nQuick bullets:\\n\\n1) Mission-critical (top 3):\\n   - Senior Inference Engineer (backfill for Aditya Rao): required for ongoing runtime optimizations tied to a customer SLA; delaying risks churn on two pilot accounts.\\n   - MLP Backend Engineer (net-new, infra team): enables autoscaling improvements to reduce per-token costs; high ROI within 6\\u20138 weeks.\\n   - Senior SRE (backfill): we are 30% under-target for on-call coverage; hiring lag is adding operational risk.\\n\\n2) Flex candidates: Mid-level SWE roles can be deprioritized or converted to contractors for Q2.\\n\\n3) If we need to pause, freeze should apply to net-new IC headcount first; backfills for critical SLAs should be exempted with approval from both you and Markus.\\n\\nI'll flag specific req IDs in the spreadsheet.\\n\\n\\u2014Vivek\\nVivek Kulkarni\\nVP Engineering\\n\\nOn Tue, Mar 10, 2026 at 09:15 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Team \\u2014\\n> \\n> As we finalize Q2 plans...\\n\",\n    \"From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>\\nTo: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>\\nDate: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze\\n\\nLaura / all \\u2014\\n\\nShort finance view:\\n\\n- Current run-rate vs plan: we're tracking ~6% above the cash flow assumption due to higher cloud spend and a couple of late professional services invoices.\\n- Hiring freeze trigger: If we cannot get run-rate back to plan within 6 weeks with cost mitigations, we should impose a temporary freeze on net-new roles. Backfills for critical operational roles (SRE, core infra, CS escalation owners) are allowed with written approval from Laura + my sign-off.\\n- Approvals: I can clear up to 4 FTEs this quarter from discretionary budget; anything beyond requires CFO/CEO approval.\\n\\nEvelyn: please mark reqs that are time-sensitive and provide expected start dates; that will help prioritize the 4 discretionary slots.\\n\\n-Markus\\nCFO (Interim)\\nMarkus Klein\\n\\nOn Tue, Mar 10, 2026 at 10:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Laura \\u2014\\n> \\n> Quick bullets:\\n\",\n    \"From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>\\nTo: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>\\nDate: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze\\n\\nHi all \\u2014\\n\\nI've updated the req tracker (attached: req_summary_Q2.pdf) and added columns: HR status, Finance status, requested start, and priority tag (Critical / High / Medium). Summary:\\n\\n- HR-approved & ready to post: 5 reqs (including Vivek's Senior Inference Engineer backfill).\\n- Pending finance sign-off: 6 reqs (mostly net-new).\\n- Time-sensitive backfills (need start by 05/01 to avoid risks): 3 reqs (SRE, Inference Eng, CS Escalation Lead).\\n\\nNotes / asks:\\n- Priya: your two reqs show as HR-approved \\u2014 if you need expedited offers, loop recruiting@peoplelogic.com (cc'd).\\n- Markus: can you confirm which of the 6 pending finance sign-offs you'd prioritize for your discretionary 4 slots?\\n\\nThanks \\u2014\\nEvelyn Hart\\nDirector, People Operations\\n\\nAttachment: req_summary_Q2.pdf (PDF stub)\\n\\nOn Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 08:47 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Laura / all \\u2014\\n\",\n    \"From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>\\nTo: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>\\nDate: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze\\n\\nLaura / team \\u2014\\n\\nAgree with Vivek and Markus on freeze semantics. Quick prioritization from my bucket:\\n\\n1) Senior Product Manager (backfill for recent departure) \\u2014 Critical: product roadmap for embeddings/infra depends on PM guidance; risk to partner commitments if not filled by mid-May.\\n2) Staff PM (net-new) \\u2014 High: strategic but can push to Q3 if needed.\\n3) Senior UX Researcher (net-new) \\u2014 Medium: nice-to-have for next-phase experiments.\\n\\nIf we get 2 discretionary slots from Markus, please prioritize the PM backfill + Vivek's Inference Eng backfill. Evelyn: I can fast-track candidate approvals this week. Recruiting is copied.\\n\\nThanks \\u2014\\nPriya Natarajan\\nHead of Product, Inference\\n\\nOn Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 12:05 PM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Hi all \\u2014\\n\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_e0ef3770372246f1b5ba2a881a0f5cc9\"\n}",
