    "From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Team —

As we finalize Q2 plans in next week's leadership sync and QBR prep, we need a quick (48h) alignment on headcount priorities and any outstanding req approvals. Key asks:

- Evelyn: can you attach the latest req spreadsheet and indicate which reqs are already HR-approved vs pending finance/headcount?
- Markus: what is the threshold for triggering a temporary hiring freeze this quarter given current spend vs plan?
- Vivek & Priya: highlight top 3 hires you consider mission-critical (backfills or net-new) and why they can't be delayed to Q3.

Context: execs are evaluating a modest contingency scenario if cloud costs stay above forecast. We want to avoid surprises in the QBR. Attached is my consolidated version of requests (headcount_request_Q2_v2.xlsx).

Please reply with short bullets (2–3 lines each). I will summarize for Friday's leadership packet.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People & Org Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: headcount_request_Q2_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
",
    "From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Laura —

Quick bullets:

1) Mission-critical (top 3):
   - Senior Inference Engineer (backfill for Aditya Rao): required for ongoing runtime optimizations tied to a customer SLA; delaying risks churn on two pilot accounts.
   - MLP Backend Engineer (net-new, infra team): enables autoscaling improvements to reduce per-token costs; high ROI within 6–8 weeks.
   - Senior SRE (backfill): we are 30% under-target for on-call coverage; hiring lag is adding operational risk.

2) Flex candidates: Mid-level SWE roles can be deprioritized or converted to contractors for Q2.

3) If we need to pause, freeze should apply to net-new IC headcount first; backfills for critical SLAs should be exempted with approval from both you and Markus.

I'll flag specific req IDs in the spreadsheet.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Engineering

> Team —
> 
> As we finalize Q2 plans...
",
    "From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Laura / all —

Short finance view:

- Current run-rate vs plan: we're tracking ~6% above the cash flow assumption due to higher cloud spend and a couple of late professional services invoices.
- Hiring freeze trigger: If we cannot get run-rate back to plan within 6 weeks with cost mitigations, we should impose a temporary freeze on net-new roles. Backfills for critical operational roles (SRE, core infra, CS escalation owners) are allowed with written approval from Laura + my sign-off.
- Approvals: I can clear up to 4 FTEs this quarter from discretionary budget; anything beyond requires CFO/CEO approval.

Evelyn: please mark reqs that are time-sensitive and provide expected start dates; that will help prioritize the 4 discretionary slots.

-Markus
CFO (Interim)
Markus Klein

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -07:00

I've updated the req tracker (attached: req_summary_Q2.pdf) and added columns: HR status, Finance status, requested start, and priority tag (Critical / High / Medium). Summary:

- HR-approved & ready to post: 5 reqs (including Vivek's Senior Inference Engineer backfill).
- Pending finance sign-off: 6 reqs (mostly net-new).
- Time-sensitive backfills (need start by 05/01 to avoid risks): 3 reqs (SRE, Inference Eng, CS Escalation Lead).

Notes / asks:
- Priya: your two reqs show as HR-approved — if you need expedited offers, loop recruiting@peoplelogic.com (cc'd).

Subject: Re: Q2 Headcount: Priority Reviews, Req Approvals & Potential Freeze

Agree with Vivek and Markus on freeze semantics. Quick prioritization from my bucket:

1) Senior Product Manager (backfill for recent departure) — Critical: product roadmap for embeddings/infra depends on PM guidance; risk to partner commitments if not filled by mid-May.

3) Senior UX Researcher (net-new) — Medium: nice-to-have for next-phase experiments.

If we get 2 discretionary slots from Markus, please prioritize the PM backfill + Vivek's Inference Eng backfill. Evelyn: I can fast-track candidate approvals this week. Recruiting is copied.

Priya Natarajan

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_fdee41e863584916a9b01d851203a0d2",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/marcus_lin/20270428-capacity-path-options-deep-scouting.json",
    "title": "Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/gmail",
    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"thread-marcus-20270428-01\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"marcus_lin\",\n  \"subject\": \"Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"marcus_lin\",\n    \"marissa_cole\",\n    \"monica_patel\",\n    \"karthik_iyer\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>\",\n    \"OliveHealth Platform <platform@olivehealth.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"4\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2027-04-28T15:20:00-07:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2027-04-30T09:14:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"sales\",\n  \"related_account\": \"OliveHealth\",\n  \"deal_id\": \"OLV-2027-073\",\n  \"region\": \"us\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"olive-traffic-sample.json\",\n    \"redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx\",\n    \"SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-olive-traces\",\n    \"HS-00045823\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai\\nDate: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700\\nSubject: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nThanks for the demo time today, Samir \\u2014 good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a short set of clarifying questions so we can size the dedicated path versus Hosted / Private VPC options: \\n\\nSummary (from today's demo)\\n- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + anonymized retrieval (low input PII, PHI-stored downstream)\\n- Latency target: interactive (sub-second p95 where possible) for the most-frequent endpoints\\n- Compliance: production data needs to be in a customer-managed VPC; non-prod can be Hosted\\n\\nClarifying questions (short answers appreciated):\\n1) Peak TPS (sustained) and short burst TPS we should plan for? (e.g., 75 TPS sustained, 200 TPS burst)\\n2) Avg/median request token mix: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, and percent that are long (>1024 tokens)\\n3) Concurrency semantics: do you need 1:1 sessions pinned, or best-effort concurrency (we optimize with batching/KV)?\\n4) P95 latency SLO for the endpoints that will be on Dedicated vs acceptable tail for Hosted fallback\\n5) Any hard requirements for KMS/BYOK, audit log retention, or region constraints beyond \\\"US\\\"?\\n\\nAttached a short sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) \\u2014 if you can drop in the traffic trace (olive-traffic-sample.json) or numbers above, we can run a quick capacity estimate and propose GPU SKU mixes (cost-first and latency-first options).\\n\\nSuggested next steps:\\n- You fill the worksheet or reply with the answers above\\n- We'll run a short projection and propose 2 SKU mixes (latency-optimized, cost-optimized) + an ops checklist for VPC onboarding\\n- If suitable, schedule a 1-hour sizing workshop next week with Ops/Infra folks\\n\\nThanks \\u2014 looping in Marissa for workshop coordination and Monica for security/compliance follow-ups.\\n\\n\\u2014 Marcus\\nMarcus Lin\\nSenior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference\\nmarcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123\\n\\nAttachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (worksheet), olive-traffic-sample.json (sample trace)\\n\",\n    \"From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>\\nTo: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai\\nCc: platform@olivehealth.com\\nDate: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:45:32 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nThanks Marcus \\u2014 appreciate the clear recap. Below are the answers (we scoped this with the infra team this morning):\\n\\n1) Traffic profile\\n- Typical daytime sustained TPS: 18 TPS across all endpoints\\n- Peak sustained TPS (end-of-month reports / campaigns): ~75 TPS sustained for 2\\u20136 hour windows\\n- Short bursts (marketing / batch jobs): up to 220 TPS for a few minutes occasionally\\n\\n2) Token mix (approx)\\n- Avg prompt tokens: 120\\n- Avg completion tokens: 250\\n- ~8% of requests exceed 1,024 tokens (mainly long summary jobs)\\n\\n3) Concurrency\\n- We expect ~20 simultaneous interactive sessions for clinical staff during peak; background jobs can be batched. We are fine with best-effort concurrency as long as p95 latency stays within SLOs for interactive endpoints.\\n\\n4) Latency SLOs\\n- Interactive endpoints: p95 <= 300ms preferred (hard requirement: <=500ms)\\n- Background summarization: p95 <= 2s is acceptable\\n\\n5) Compliance / security\\n- Production must run in our VPC (customer-managed) with KMS BYOK for encryption at rest; non-prod can be hosted.\\n- SOC2 required; attaching a pointer to our security intake (SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf) and the platform team's contact (platform@olivehealth.com).\\n\\nTimeline: aim to move to an initial Dedicated pilot in 6\\u20138 weeks if the sizing checks out.\\n\\nI uploaded a week of representative traces to the drive link you gave (folder: 1a2b3c-olive-traces). Let me know if you need raw logs or anonymized request bodies.\\n\\n\\u2014 Samir\\nSamir Khan\\nHead of Platform Engineering, OliveHealth\\nsamir.khan@olivehealth.com\\n\\nAttachments: SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf\\n\",\n    \"From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica.patel@redwood.ai\\nDate: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:10:04 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nGreat dataset \\u2014 thanks Samir, this is exactly what we need. Quick read and our initial take + proposed plan: \\n\\nInitial sizing thoughts (high level)\\n- Given the 75 TPS peak + 220 TPS short bursts and your p95 <= 300ms target for interactive endpoints, we recommend starting with a Dedicated pool that emphasizes latency with an ops-safe fallback to Hosted variants for non-critical traffic.\\n- Two SKU mixes we'll model: \\n  A) Latency-optimized: 4 x A100-80GB inference nodes (low-latency kernels, larger KV cache). This favors lower p95 at higher cost.\\n  B) Cost-optimized: 12 x A10G-style inference nodes with aggressive batching and prefix caching to hit sustained 75 TPS at lower cost, with occasional burst scaling to handle short spikes.\\n\\nNotes on architecture and tradeoffs\\n- KV/prefix caching will reduce token compute on repeated contexts (clinical templates) \\u2014 this benefits A10G options more for cost savings.\\n- Heavy long-tail requests (>1k tokens) will push memory needs; the A100-80GB config gives headroom for those workloads without model splits.\\n- For your BYOK/KMS requirement and VPC onboarding: our Private deployment (VPC/private control plane) supports customer-managed keys and audit log forwarding; Monica will follow up with the security checklist for the procurement team.\\n\\nImmediate next steps (proposed)\\n1) Marcus + I run the sizing worksheet you filled and convert traces to token-level projections (we'll do that today).\\n2) Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop next Tue or Wed with your infra + security (we're flexible) \\u2014 proposed slots: Tue May 4 10:00\\u201311:00 PT or Wed May 5 13:00\\u201314:00 PT.\\n3) If the team is comfortable with the projection, we'll spin a short Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) with monitoring hooks and rollback to Hosted for non-prod traffic.\\n\\nAction items: Samir \\u2014 confirm which workshop slot works and attach the worksheet populated if convenient. Monica \\u2014 I flagged security checklist and BYOK runbook (see related Drive link).\\n\\nThanks \\u2014 happy to jump on a call to walk through the two SKU mixes once Marcus has the projection ready.\\n\\n\\u2014 Marissa\\nMarissa Cole\\nEnterprise AE, Redwood Inference\\nmarissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199\\n\\nAttachments referenced: proposed-ops-runbook.md (link in Drive)\\n\",\n    \"From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>\\nDate: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-demo recap \\u2014 deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications\\n\\nQuick note from infra: sounds good to me \\u2014 if you confirm the sample traces are representative we'll prioritize a capacity projection and a short benchmark (we'll exercise both SKU mixes under a synthetic traffic profile).\\n\\nKarthik\\nKarthik Iyer\\nDirector, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference\\n\",\n    \"-- End of thread --\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_fdee41e863584916a9b01d851203a0d2\"\n}",

  "messages": [
    "From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Thanks for the demo time today, Samir — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a short set of clarifying questions so we can size the dedicated path versus Hosted / Private VPC options: 

Summary (from today's demo)
- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + anonymized retrieval (low input PII, PHI-stored downstream)
- Latency target: interactive (sub-second p95 where possible) for the most-frequent endpoints
- Compliance: production data needs to be in a customer-managed VPC; non-prod can be Hosted

Clarifying questions (short answers appreciated):
1) Peak TPS (sustained) and short burst TPS we should plan for? (e.g., 75 TPS sustained, 200 TPS burst)
2) Avg/median request token mix: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, and percent that are long (>1024 tokens)
3) Concurrency semantics: do you need 1:1 sessions pinned, or best-effort concurrency (we optimize with batching/KV)?
4) P95 latency SLO for the endpoints that will be on Dedicated vs acceptable tail for Hosted fallback
5) Any hard requirements for KMS/BYOK, audit log retention, or region constraints beyond "US"?

Attached a short sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — if you can drop in the traffic trace (olive-traffic-sample.json) or numbers above, we can run a quick capacity estimate and propose GPU SKU mixes (cost-first and latency-first options).

Suggested next steps:
- You fill the worksheet or reply with the answers above
- We'll run a short projection and propose 2 SKU mixes (latency-optimized, cost-optimized) + an ops checklist for VPC onboarding
- If suitable, schedule a 1-hour sizing workshop next week with Ops/Infra folks

Thanks — looping in Marissa for workshop coordination and Monica for security/compliance follow-ups.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (worksheet), olive-traffic-sample.json (sample trace)
",
    "From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@olivehealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:45:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. Below are the answers (we scoped this with the infra team this morning):

1) Traffic profile
- Typical daytime sustained TPS: 18 TPS across all endpoints
- Peak sustained TPS (end-of-month reports / campaigns): ~75 TPS sustained for 2–6 hour windows
- Short bursts (marketing / batch jobs): up to 220 TPS for a few minutes occasionally

2) Token mix (approx)
- Avg prompt tokens: 120
- Avg completion tokens: 250
- ~8% of requests exceed 1,024 tokens (mainly long summary jobs)

3) Concurrency
- We expect ~20 simultaneous interactive sessions for clinical staff during peak; background jobs can be batched. We are fine with best-effort concurrency as long as p95 latency stays within SLOs for interactive endpoints.

4) Latency SLOs
- Interactive endpoints: p95 <= 300ms preferred (hard requirement: <=500ms)
- Background summarization: p95 <= 2s is acceptable

5) Compliance / security
- Production must run in our VPC (customer-managed) with KMS BYOK for encryption at rest; non-prod can be hosted.
- SOC2 required; attaching a pointer to our security intake (SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf) and the platform team's contact (platform@olivehealth.com).

Timeline: aim to move to an initial Dedicated pilot in 6–8 weeks if the sizing checks out.

I uploaded a week of representative traces to the drive link you gave (folder: 1a2b3c-olive-traces). Let me know if you need raw logs or anonymized request bodies.

— Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, OliveHealth
samir.khan@olivehealth.com

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf
",
    "From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:10:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Great dataset — thanks Samir, this is exactly what we need. Quick read and our initial take + proposed plan: 

Initial sizing thoughts (high level)
- Given the 75 TPS peak + 220 TPS short bursts and your p95 <= 300ms target for interactive endpoints, we recommend starting with a Dedicated pool that emphasizes latency with an ops-safe fallback to Hosted variants for non-critical traffic.
- Two SKU mixes we'll model: 
  A) Latency-optimized: 4 x A100-80GB inference nodes (low-latency kernels, larger KV cache). This favors lower p95 at higher cost.
  B) Cost-optimized: 12 x A10G-style inference nodes with aggressive batching and prefix caching to hit sustained 75 TPS at lower cost, with occasional burst scaling to handle short spikes.

Notes on architecture and tradeoffs
- KV/prefix caching will reduce token compute on repeated contexts (clinical templates) — this benefits A10G options more for cost savings.
- Heavy long-tail requests (>1k tokens) will push memory needs; the A100-80GB config gives headroom for those workloads without model splits.
- For your BYOK/KMS requirement and VPC onboarding: our Private deployment (VPC/private control plane) supports customer-managed keys and audit log forwarding; Monica will follow up with the security checklist for the procurement team.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Marcus + I run the sizing worksheet you filled and convert traces to token-level projections (we'll do that today).
2) Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop next Tue or Wed with your infra + security (we're flexible) — proposed slots: Tue May 4 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed May 5 13:00–14:00 PT.
3) If the team is comfortable with the projection, we'll spin a short Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) with monitoring hooks and rollback to Hosted for non-prod traffic.

Action items: Samir — confirm which workshop slot works and attach the worksheet populated if convenient. Monica — I flagged security checklist and BYOK runbook (see related Drive link).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the two SKU mixes once Marcus has the projection ready.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments referenced: proposed-ops-runbook.md (link in Drive)
",

To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Quick note from infra: sounds good to me — if you confirm the sample traces are representative we'll prioritize a capacity projection and a short benchmark (we'll exercise both SKU mixes under a synthetic traffic profile).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference

    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Release Bridge Call \\u2014 Playback & Risk Scan (2025-02-18)\",\n  \"owner\": \"Maya Patel\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/release-bridge-call-playback-and-risk-scan.json\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-18\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2025-02-21\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Alejandro Ruiz\",\n    \"Chen Li\",\n    \"Priya Nair\",\n    \"Derek O'Neal\",\n    \"Samira Haddad\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"eng-release-engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"in_review\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"release-bridge\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"hotfix\",\n    \"risk-scan\",\n    \"runtime-v2.4.1\",\n    \"kv-cache\",\n    \"post-deploy\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RELEASE-987\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2347\",\n    \"confluence://pages/release-bridge-checklist\",\n    \"slack://channel/release-bridge-thread-FFX9\"\n  ],\n  \"summary\": \"Playback of the 02/18 release bridge call covering runtime v2.4.1 rollout plan, CANARY run in us-east-1, hotfix candidates, and a rapid risk-scan for known unknowns. Primary goal: staged release with safe rollback options if KV cache latency or tokenization regression reappears. This doc captures decisions, open questions, and owners for the next 72 hours.\",\n  \"attendees\": [\n    \"Maya Patel (Release Lead)\",\n    \"Alejandro Ruiz (Serving Runtime)\",\n    \"Chen Li (SRE)\",\n    \"Priya Nair (Product Ops)\",\n    \"Derek O'Neal (QA)\",\n    \"Samira Haddad (Solutions Eng)\",\n    \"TBD (Oncall)\"\n  ],\n  \"agenda\": [\n    \"Quick health check and known incidents\",\n    \"Canary configuration and target metrics\",\n    \"Hotfix and rollback readiness\",\n    \"Risk scan (top 6 risks)\",\n    \"Action items and notifier/responsibilities\",\n    \"Follow-up timing\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": \"09:05 PST start. Quick state: production stable overnight; sporadic CPU spikes reported in eu-west-1 (investigating separate). Release window approved 10:00\\u201314:00 PST. Runtime v2.4.1 includes attention optimization, KV-cache prefetch change, and batching tweak.\\n\\nCanary plan: 2 canary hosts in us-east-1 behind the regular LB, target 5% of incoming traffic for first 30 minutes, then 20% for next 60 minutes if metrics stable. Metrics to watch: p95 latency, token/second throughput, error rate, model output divergence score (auto-eval on a small prompt set). Canary gating thresholds: p95 < 130ms (+10% baseline), error-rate < 0.5%, divergence delta < 2.5 BLEU-equivalent metric.\\n\\nObserved regression vector: the KV-cache prefetch change reduced cold-start latency but introduced a slow warmup path for long-sequence requests. QA reproduced the slow-warmup at scale in staging: median warmup time 2.9s (target <1.2s) when sequence>2048. Mitigation discussed: pre-warm script to prime KV entries before traffic shift and temporarily increase kv-prefetch-batch-size. Alejandro to prepare canary environment with pre-warm hook.\\n\\nHotfix candidates: PR #2347 (revert aggressive prefetch heuristics) is ready for fast patch. If canary p95 > 150ms or error-rate spikes > 1.0% in first 30 minutes, immediate action: revert to previous prefetch heuristics (hotfix path A) and shift canary traffic back to 0% while scaling classic runtime pool. Escalation: call SRE lead and release lead; page oncall.\\n\\nRollout decisions: proceed with staged canary today per plan. Hold condition: any model-output regression above threshold or persistent kv-warmup > 1.5s after pre-warm attempt. If hold occurs, open incident and break release for deeper analysis.\\n\\nCommunications: update #release-bridge Slack with minute-by-minute short bullets during rollout. Customer-facing status page will be updated only if rollback occurs or customer-impacting errors detected.\\n\\nOpen questions captured during call: 1) Are there any downstream consumers of the KV cache that rely on ordering semantics changed by prefetch? (Action: Priya to confirm with model-onboarding team). 2) Can we synthetic-exercise heavy long-sequence workload on canary before shifting live traffic? (Action: Derek to run load script).\",\n  \"risk_scan\": [\n    \"KV-cache warmup regression (Severity: High) \\u2014 Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: pre-warm hook + fallback revert PR #2347. Owner: Alejandro. Contingency: rollback within 10 minutes.\",\n    \"Model tokenization divergence (Severity: High) \\u2014 Likelihood: Low but impact high. Mitigation: run quick eval set during canary; if divergence > threshold, abort. Owner: Derek.\",\n    \"Autoscale lag under burst (Severity: Medium) \\u2014 Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: pre-provision burst capacity in us-east-1 for release window. Owner: Chen.\",\n    \"Config drift between regions (Severity: Medium) \\u2014 Likelihood: Low. Mitigation: checksum of runtime configs pre-rollout. Owner: Maya.\",\n    \"Monitoring breakage / missing traces (Severity: Medium) \\u2014 Likelihood: Low. Mitigation: sanity check telemetry pipelines 30m before shift. Owner: Samira.\",\n    \"Customer-visible higher cost due to mis-batching (Severity: Low) \\u2014 Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: revert batching flag if cost/perf delta > 15%. Owner: Product Ops (Priya).\"\n  ],\n  \"action_items\": [\n    \"Alejandro: Prepare canary hosts with pre-warm hook + deploy runtime v2.4.1 to canary (due 2025-02-18 09:45 PST)\",\n    \"Derek: Run long-sequence synthetic load on canary (script: load-longseq-v3) and post results to this doc (due 2025-02-18 09:30 PST)\",\n    \"Chen: Provision + confirm burst capacity in us-east-1 and validate autoscaler lookback window (due 2025-02-18 09:50 PST)\",\n    \"Priya: Confirm no downstream ordering dependencies in model-onboarding/team and update linked artifact if there are (due 2025-02-18 09:40 PST)\",\n    \"Samira: Run telemetry sanity check for traces, metrics, and logs; confirm dashboards are receiving canary tags (due 2025-02-18 09:35 PST)\",\n    \"Maya: Publish minute-by-minute Slack guide and hold contact list; be primary comms until handoff (due 2025-02-18 09:15 PST)\",\n    \"Maya: If rollback triggered, open incident in PagerDuty and file postmortem stub (due immediate on rollback)\",\n    \"All: Confirm readiness in #release-bridge 10 minutes prior to shift (due 2025-02-18 09:50 PST)\"\n  ],\n  \"change_log_summary\": [\n    \"runtime v2.4.1: attention kernel micro-optimizations (+6-9% throughput on short context),\\nkv-cache prefetch change to reduce cold-starts, batch sizing tweak for cont-batching\",\n    \"config flags: kv-prefetch-batch-size default bumped from 8->24 in v2.4.1 (can be overridden at runtime via feature flag)\",\n    \"metric hooks: added model-output-divergence quick-eval endpoint and canary tagging headers\",\n    \"packaging: new docker base image with glibc 2.36 (minor OS-level perf gain)\"\n  ],\n  \"follow_up_meeting\": \"If rollout succeeds, quick sync 2025-02-18 15:30 PST to confirm metrics and close ticket. document.title: Release Bridge Call — Playback & Risk Scan (2025-02-18)
document.content:
{
  "title": "Release Bridge Call \u2014 Playback & Risk Scan (2025-02-18)",
  "owner": "Maya Patel",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/release-bridge-call-playback-and-risk-scan.json",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2025-02-18",
  "last_modified": "2025-02-21",
  "collaborators": [
    "Alejandro Ruiz",
    "Chen Li",
    "Priya Nair",
    "Derek O'Neal",
    "Samira Haddad"
  ],
  "team": "eng-release-engineering",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "release-bridge",
    "canary",
    "hotfix",
    "risk-scan",
    "runtime-v2.4.1",
    "kv-cache",
    "post-deploy"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RELEASE-987",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2347",
    "confluence://pages/release-bridge-checklist",
    "slack://channel/release-bridge-thread-FFX9"
  ],
  "summary": "Playback of the 02/18 release bridge call covering runtime v2.4.1 rollout plan, CANARY run in us-east-1, hotfix candidates, and a rapid risk-scan for known unknowns. Primary goal: staged release with safe rollback options if KV cache latency or tokenization regression reappears. This doc captures decisions, open questions, and owners for the next 72 hours.",
  "attendees": [
    "Maya Patel (Release Lead)",
    "Alejandro Ruiz (Serving Runtime)",
    "Chen Li (SRE)",
    "Priya Nair (Product Ops)",
    "Derek O'Neal (QA)",
    "Samira Haddad (Solutions Eng)",
    "TBD (Oncall)"
  ],
  "agenda": [
    "Quick health check and known incidents",
    "Canary configuration and target metrics",
    "Hotfix and rollback readiness",
    "Risk scan (top 6 risks)",
    "Action items and notifier/responsibilities",
    "Follow-up timing"
  ],
  "notes": "09:05 PST start. Quick state: production stable overnight; sporadic CPU spikes reported in eu-west-1 (investigating separate). Release window approved 10:00\u201314:00 PST. Runtime v2.4.1 includes attention optimization, KV-cache prefetch change, and batching tweak.\n\nCanary plan: 2 canary hosts in us-east-1 behind the regular LB, target 5% of incoming traffic for first 30 minutes, then 20% for next 60 minutes if metrics stable. Metrics to watch: p95 latency, token/second throughput, error rate, model output divergence score (auto-eval on a small prompt set). Canary gating thresholds: p95 < 130ms (+10% baseline), error-rate < 0.5%, divergence delta < 2.5 BLEU-equivalent metric.\n\nObserved regression vector: the KV-cache prefetch change reduced cold-start latency but introduced a slow warmup path for long-sequence requests. QA reproduced the slow-warmup at scale in staging: median warmup time 2.9s (target <1.2s) when sequence>2048. Mitigation discussed: pre-warm script to prime KV entries before traffic shift and temporarily increase kv-prefetch-batch-size. Alejandro to prepare canary environment with pre-warm hook.\n\nHotfix candidates: PR #2347 (revert aggressive prefetch heuristics) is ready for fast patch. If canary p95 > 150ms or error-rate spikes > 1.0% in first 30 minutes, immediate action: revert to previous prefetch heuristics (hotfix path A) and shift canary traffic back to 0% while scaling classic runtime pool. Escalation: call SRE lead and release lead; page oncall.\n\nRollout decisions: proceed with staged canary today per plan. Hold condition: any model-output regression above threshold or persistent kv-warmup > 1.5s after pre-warm attempt. If hold occurs, open incident and break release for deeper analysis.\n\nCommunications: update #release-bridge Slack with minute-by-minute short bullets during rollout. Customer-facing status page will be updated only if rollback occurs or customer-impacting errors detected.\n\nOpen questions captured during call: 1) Are there any downstream consumers of the KV cache that rely on ordering semantics changed by prefetch? (Action: Priya to confirm with model-onboarding team). 2) Can we synthetic-exercise heavy long-sequence workload on canary before shifting live traffic? (Action: Derek to run load script).",
  "risk_scan": [
    "KV-cache warmup regression (Severity: High) \u2014 Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: pre-warm hook + fallback revert PR #2347. Owner: Alejandro. Contingency: rollback within 10 minutes.",
    "Model tokenization divergence (Severity: High) \u2014 Likelihood: Low but impact high. Mitigation: run quick eval set during canary; if divergence > threshold, abort. Owner: Derek.",
    "Autoscale lag under burst (Severity: Medium) \u2014 Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: pre-provision burst capacity in us-east-1 for release window. Owner: Chen.",
    "Config drift between regions (Severity: Medium) \u2014 Likelihood: Low. Mitigation: checksum of runtime configs pre-rollout. Owner: Maya.",
    "Monitoring breakage / missing traces (Severity: Medium) \u2014 Likelihood: Low. Mitigation: sanity check telemetry pipelines 30m before shift. Owner: Samira.",
    "Customer-visible higher cost due to mis-batching (Severity: Low) \u2014 Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: revert batching flag if cost/perf delta > 15%. Owner: Product Ops (Priya)."
  ],
  "action_items": [
    "Alejandro: Prepare canary hosts with pre-warm hook + deploy runtime v2.4.1 to canary (due 2025-02-18 09:45 PST)",
    "Derek: Run long-sequence synthetic load on canary (script: load-longseq-v3) and post results to this doc (due 2025-02-18 09:30 PST)",
    "Chen: Provision + confirm burst capacity in us-east-1 and validate autoscaler lookback window (due 2025-02-18 09:50 PST)",
    "Priya: Confirm no downstream ordering dependencies in model-onboarding/team and update linked artifact if there are (due 2025-02-18 09:40 PST)",
    "Samira: Run telemetry sanity check for traces, metrics, and logs; confirm dashboards are receiving canary tags (due 2025-02-18 09:35 PST)",
    "Maya: Publish minute-by-minute Slack guide and hold contact list; be primary comms until handoff (due 2025-02-18 09:15 PST)",
    "Maya: If rollback triggered, open incident in PagerDuty and file postmortem stub (due immediate on rollback)",
    "All: Confirm readiness in #release-bridge 10 minutes prior to shift (due 2025-02-18 09:50 PST)"
  ],
  "change_log_summary": [
    "runtime v2.4.1: attention kernel micro-optimizations (+6-9% throughput on short context),\nkv-cache prefetch change to reduce cold-starts, batch sizing tweak for cont-batching",
    "config flags: kv-prefetch-batch-size default bumped from 8->24 in v2.4.1 (can be overridden at runtime via feature flag)",
    "metric hooks: added model-output-divergence quick-eval endpoint and canary tagging headers",
    "packaging: new docker base image with glibc 2.36 (minor OS-level perf gain)"
  ],
  "follow_up_meeting": "If rollout succeeds, quick sync 2025-02-18 15:30 PST to confirm metrics and close ticket. If rollback occurs, convene incident review within 48 hours.",
  "post_notes": "Post-call: Derek found a flaky test that overestimated warmup time; adjusted load script and re-ran. Alejandro pushed canary with pre-warm hook and initial synthetic passed. Monitoring flagged a transient p95 blip at 10:12 PST \u2014 investigated, attributed to queue backlog in lb; spin-up of extra canary host cleared backlog. No rollback performed. Will track extended warmup regression in the 48h window.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "summary",
    "notes",
    "risk_scan",
    "action_items",
    "change_log_summary",
    "follow_up_meeting",
    "post_notes"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_c15dcd05b9ab4628ae30216950b1a435"
}

root cause : two independent failures coincided and amplified impact : ( 1 ) a model rollout ( reranker v3. 1 ) contained a preprocessing tokenizer change that produced shifted embedding vectors for edge - case inputs, producing a measurable recall regression. ( 2 ) an autoscaler termination - healthcheck regression ( introduced in autoscaler v1. 14 ) caused gpu pods to be killed and recreated under load rather than gracefully draining, creating cache churn and transient ooms which increased latency and reduced capacity.

    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json",
    "title": "Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\",\n  \"space\": \"applied-ml-and-evals\",\n  \"author\": \"Anjali Mehta\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-11-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-01-08\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Evan Park\",\n    \"Luis Ortega\",\n    \"Marina Cole\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"regression-triage\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"rollout-policy\",\n    \"probe-heatmap\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026\",\n    \"/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n-------\\nThis document defines a reproducible protocol to convert probe heatmaps (telemetry-driven failure density views) into rollout decisions for model promotions, quantization migrations, and configuration changes. The goal is to make decisions auditable, time-bounded, and aligned with SLOs so product and ops can act consistently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\\n\\nScope\\n-----\\n- Applies to any promotion or rollout that is gated by probe-driven quality signals: model promotions, quantized rollouts, prompt rewrites, and routing policy changes.\\n- Focuses on probe heatmaps produced by the eval harness and live shadow probes (not human labelling pipelines).\\n- Excludes legislated/regulatory decisions (finance/compliance) - see separate compliance approval flow.\\n\\nKey definitions\\n---------------\\n- Probe heatmap: a time-windowed 2D histogram where rows are probes (slice identifiers) and columns are failure modes (fidelity, hallucination, latency, embeddings drift). Each cell contains count and a severity score.\\n- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.\\n- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).\\n\\nInputs required\\n---------------\\n1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.\\n2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.\\n3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).\\n4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).\\n5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.\\n\\nDecision scoring algorithm (summary)\\n----------------------------------\\nWe compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):\\n\\n- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)\\n- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30\\n- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift\\n\\nFinal Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)\\n\\nAction mapping (recommended)\\n---------------------------\\n- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)\\n- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)\\n- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)\\n- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)\\n\\nConfiguration table (defaults)\\n-----------------------------\\n- heatmap_window_hours: 24 -- Time window to compute the snapshot\\n- probe_priority_weights: CriticalTenantFlows:10, BillingIntents:8, UXTextGen:3 -- Priority map used in SS\\n- latency_slo_ms: 250 -- latency SLO used for LP calculation\\n- drift_baseline_window_days: 7 -- Days used to compute baseline drift\\n- slow_roll_threshold: 35 -- DS threshold to switch to slow rollout\\n- human_review_timeout_hours: 4 -- Max time to complete targeted review\\n\\nOwnership and roles\\n-------------------\\n- Eval Oncall (primary): validates heatmap integrity, runs automated bisect and approves/requests human review.\\n- Model Owner (secondary): responsible for quick triage of failing slices and submitting patch/rollforward.\\n- Release Engineer: executes percent traffic adjustments and rollbacks in the serving control plane.\\n- Oncall Platform SRE: monitors capacity/latency regressions and authorizes emergency rollbacks for tail latency incidents.\\n\\nProcedure: from snapshot to decision (operational runbook)\\n------------------------------------------------------\\n1. Fetch heatmap snapshot and baseline. Verify telemetry completeness (missing probes < 5% of expected).\\n2. Run validation script to confirm probe schema and timestamps: 'python tools/heatmap_validate.py --snapshot /tmp/heatmap.json'\\n3. Compute DS using the scoring algorithm and emit a decision document to /incidents/probe-decisions/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.json. Example: curl -X POST 'https://ops-api.internal/decisions' -d '{'ds': 27, 'action': 'CAUTION', 'top_slices': ['BillingIntents:charge-failure'] }'\\n4. If action == GO: continue rollout. Log event and schedule a 24h follow-up check.\\n5. If action == CAUTION: cap rollout at 10% for 6 hours, assign Model Owner and Eval Oncall for targeted human validation, and run automated bisect on top 5 degrading slices.\\n6. If action == HOLD: pause rollout, mark the release as blocked in release tracker, and create a regression investigation ticket with pre-populated triage fields.\\n7. If action == ROLLBACK: trigger automated rollback playbook and notify the incident channel #regression-ops with summary and rollback links.\\n\\nAutomated bisect integration\\n---------------------------\\n- The decision pipeline calls the bisect service with the top N probes by (failure_count * avg_severity). The bisect run ID is included in the decision document.\\n- If bisect identifies a single suspect change (probability > 0.7) the Model Owner must decide to either patch or rollback within human_review_timeout_hours.\\n\\nTelemetry contract (minimal required fields)\\n-----------------------------------------\\nEmitters must provide a compact heatmap JSON with the following fields (example snippet):\\n\\n'{'\\n  'snapshot_ts': '2025-01-08T08:00:00Z',\\n  'window_hours': 24,\\n  'slices': [\\n    {\\n      'slice_id': 'BillingIntents:charge-failure',\\n      'total_calls': 12450,\\n      'failure_count': 312,\\n      'avg_severity': 2.8,\\n      'median_latency_ms': 430,\\n      'embedding_drift_score': 0.34\\n    }\\n  ]\\n}'\\n\\nRequired export fields (flat): snapshot_ts, window_hours, slices[].slice_id, slices[].total_calls, slices[].failure_count, slices[].avg_severity, slices[].median_latency_ms, slices[].embedding_drift_score. Optional: host_cluster, model_variant, tenant_id.\\n\\nSafety checks and hard gates\\n---------------------------\\n- If any CriticalTenantFlows slice has failure_rate > 0.5% AND avg_severity >= 3.0 the system must ROLLBACK regardless of DS.\\n- If more than 10% of probes lack current telemetry, mark decision state as INCONCLUSIVE and require human approval.\\n- For private/on-prem customers with per-customer SLO overrides, consult the customer SLO manifest before automatic rollback - use the per-customer override endpoint.\\n\\nRollback criteria and runbook steps\\n----------------------------------\\n1. Lock the rollout in the control plane: 'redwoodctl rollout lock --id <rollout-id>'\\n2. Execute the variant revert: 'redwoodctl rollout revert --id <rollout-id> --target <baseline-model>'\\n3. Post-rollback verification: run a 2-hour fast-probe sweep across top 20 slices and confirm DS falls below 20.\\n4. Create incident with severity mapping: DS>80 -> Sev2, DS 60-80 -> Sev3.\\n\\nExample: case study (short)\\n-------------------------\\n- Scenario: Quantized v1.2 was promoted to 20% across US-hosted tenants. After 12 hours heatmap snapshot showed elevated embedding_drift_score in 3 billing-related slices. Computed DS = 42 -> HOLD. Automated bisect pointed to a tokenizer change in the preprocessor. Model Owner rolled back quant patch and re-run priming probes; DS dropped to 12 within 3 hours and rollout resumed at a slow cadence.\\n\\nAppendix A: configuration YAML sample\\n------------------------------------\\n'heatmap_window_hours: 24\\nprobe_priority_weights:\\n  CriticalTenantFlows: 10\\n  BillingIntents: 8\\n  UXTextGen: 3\\nlatency_slo_ms: 250\\ndrift_baseline_window_days: 7\\nslow_roll_threshold: 35\\nhuman_review_timeout_hours: 4'\\n\\nAppendix B: links and references\\n--------------------------------\\n- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026\\n- Regression prioritization index: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024\\n\\nAppendix C: change history\\n--------------------------\\n- 2024-11-12 (Anjali Mehta): First draft and internal review.\\n- 2024-12-02 (Evan Park): Added bisect integration details and telemetry contract.\\n- 2025-01-08 (Marina Cole): Clarified safety gates for private deployments and updated example.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_b4bd83b46612452e858bc02b380082e2\"\n}",

{
  "title": "Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol",
  "space": "applied-ml-and-evals",
  "author": "Anjali Mehta",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-11-12",
  "last_updated": "2025-01-08",
  "reviewers": [
    "Evan Park",
    "Luis Ortega",
    "Marina Cole"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "regression-triage",
    "telemetry",
    "rollout-policy",
    "probe-heatmap"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026",
    "/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024"
  ],
  "content": "Summary
-------
This document defines a reproducible protocol to convert probe heatmaps (telemetry-driven failure density views) into rollout decisions for model promotions, quantization migrations, and configuration changes. The goal is to make decisions auditable, time-bounded, and aligned with SLOs so product and ops can act consistently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
-----
- Applies to any promotion or rollout that is gated by probe-driven quality signals: model promotions, quantized rollouts, prompt rewrites, and routing policy changes.
- Focuses on probe heatmaps produced by the eval harness and live shadow probes (not human labelling pipelines).
- Excludes legislated/regulatory decisions (finance/compliance) - see separate compliance approval flow.

Key definitions
---------------
- Probe heatmap: a time-windowed 2D histogram where rows are probes (slice identifiers) and columns are failure modes (fidelity, hallucination, latency, embeddings drift). Each cell contains count and a severity score.
- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.
- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).

Inputs required
---------------
1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.
2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.
3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).
4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).
5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.

Decision scoring algorithm (summary)
----------------------------------
We compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):

- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)
- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30
- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift

Final Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)

Action mapping (recommended)
---------------------------
- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)
- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)
- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)
- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)

Configuration table (defaults)
-----------------------------
- heatmap_window_hours: 24 -- Time window to compute the snapshot
- probe_priority_weights: CriticalTenantFlows:10, BillingIntents:8, UXTextGen:3 -- Priority map used in SS
- latency_slo_ms: 250 -- latency SLO used for LP calculation
- drift_baseline_window_days: 7 -- Days used to compute baseline drift
- slow_roll_threshold: 35 -- DS threshold to switch to slow rollout
- human_review_timeout_hours: 4 -- Max time to complete targeted review

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Eval Oncall (primary): validates heatmap integrity, runs automated bisect and approves/requests human review.
- Model Owner (secondary): responsible for quick triage of failing slices and submitting patch/rollforward.
- Release Engineer: executes percent traffic adjustments and rollbacks in the serving control plane.
- Oncall Platform SRE: monitors capacity/latency regressions and authorizes emergency rollbacks for tail latency incidents.

Procedure: from snapshot to decision (operational runbook)
------------------------------------------------------
1. Fetch heatmap snapshot and baseline. Verify telemetry completeness (missing probes < 5% of expected).
2. Run validation script to confirm probe schema and timestamps: 'python tools/heatmap_validate.py --snapshot /tmp/heatmap.json'
3. Compute DS using the scoring algorithm and emit a decision document to /incidents/probe-decisions/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.json. Example: curl -X POST 'https://ops-api.internal/decisions' -d '{'ds': 27, 'action': 'CAUTION', 'top_slices': ['BillingIntents:charge-failure'] }'
4. If action == GO: continue rollout. Log event and schedule a 24h follow-up check.
5. If action == CAUTION: cap rollout at 10% for 6 hours, assign Model Owner and Eval Oncall for targeted human validation, and run automated bisect on top 5 degrading slices.
6. If action == HOLD: pause rollout, mark the release as blocked in release tracker, and create a regression investigation ticket with pre-populated triage fields.
7. If action == ROLLBACK: trigger automated rollback playbook and notify the incident channel #regression-ops with summary and rollback links.

Automated bisect integration
---------------------------
- The decision pipeline calls the bisect service with the top N probes by (failure_count * avg_severity). The bisect run ID is included in the decision document.
- If bisect identifies a single suspect change (probability > 0.7) the Model Owner must decide to either patch or rollback within human_review_timeout_hours.

Telemetry contract (minimal required fields)
-----------------------------------------
Emitters must provide a compact heatmap JSON with the following fields (example snippet):

'{'
  'snapshot_ts': '2025-01-08T08:00:00Z',
  'window_hours': 24,
  'slices': [
    {
      'slice_id': 'BillingIntents:charge-failure',
      'total_calls': 12450,
      'failure_count': 312,
      'avg_severity': 2.8,
      'median_latency_ms': 430,
      'embedding_drift_score': 0.34
    }
  ]
}'

Required export fields (flat): snapshot_ts, window_hours, slices[].slice_id, slices[].total_calls, slices[].failure_count, slices[].avg_severity, slices[].median_latency_ms, slices[].embedding_drift_score. Optional: host_cluster, model_variant, tenant_id.

Safety checks and hard gates
---------------------------
- If any CriticalTenantFlows slice has failure_rate > 0.5% AND avg_severity >= 3.0 the system must ROLLBACK regardless of DS.
- If more than 10% of probes lack current telemetry, mark decision state as INCONCLUSIVE and require human approval.
- For private/on-prem customers with per-customer SLO overrides, consult the customer SLO manifest before automatic rollback - use the per-customer override endpoint.

Rollback criteria and runbook steps
----------------------------------
1. Lock the rollout in the control plane: 'redwoodctl rollout lock --id <rollout-id>'
2. Execute the variant revert: 'redwoodctl rollout revert --id <rollout-id> --target <baseline-model>'
3. Post-rollback verification: run a 2-hour fast-probe sweep across top 20 slices and confirm DS falls below 20.
4. Create incident with severity mapping: DS>80 -> Sev2, DS 60-80 -> Sev3.

Example: case study (short)
-------------------------
- Scenario: Quantized v1.2 was promoted to 20% across US-hosted tenants. After 12 hours heatmap snapshot showed elevated embedding_drift_score in 3 billing-related slices. Computed DS = 42 -> HOLD. Automated bisect pointed to a tokenizer change in the preprocessor. Model Owner rolled back quant patch and re-run priming probes; DS dropped to 12 within 3 hours and rollout resumed at a slow cadence.

Appendix A: configuration YAML sample
------------------------------------
'heatmap_window_hours: 24
probe_priority_weights:
  CriticalTenantFlows: 10
  BillingIntents: 8
  UXTextGen: 3
latency_slo_ms: 250
drift_baseline_window_days: 7
slow_roll_threshold: 35
human_review_timeout_hours: 4'

Appendix B: links and references
--------------------------------
- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Regression prioritization index: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024

Appendix C: change history
--------------------------
- 2024-11-12 (Anjali Mehta): First draft and internal review.
- 2024-12-02 (Evan Park): Added bisect integration details and telemetry contract.
- 2025-01-08 (Marina Cole): Clarified safety gates for private deployments and updated example.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "content"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_b4bd83b46612452e858bc02b380082e2"
}

# EnterpriseRAG evidence reconciliation procedure

## Purpose

This procedure makes each answer reproducible from branch-visible Redwood knowledge while preventing answer leakage and cross-question contamination.

## Repeatable method

1. **Create an isolated branch.** Check out a unique task branch from the named person/team branch and use that branch ID for every subsequent operation.
2. **Resolve each question independently.** Convert one question at a time into a narrow semantic query containing its distinctive nouns, identifiers, version strings, and requested relationship. Do not seed a query with conclusions from another question.
3. **Resolve identifiers before synthesis.** Treat exact version numbers, ticket keys, ADR numbers, customer/deployment names, and protocol frame names as join keys. Prefer a result whose title and body both match. Use cross-system references only to locate corroboration, never as evidence by themselves.
4. **Fetch full sources when snippets are incomplete.** Fetch the complete document when a passage truncates a command sequence, formula, timeline, field list, exception, or decision context. Cite the complete document's stable ID and corpus path.
5. **Rank authority and specificity.** Prefer final ADRs and merged implementation records for normative technical behavior; incident/root-cause tickets for causes; approved leadership email for policy timing; product requirements for eligibility; and meeting transcripts for explicitly agreed follow-ups. Drafts remain usable when the question explicitly asks about a draft.
6. **Reconcile conflicts explicitly.** Compare date/status, scope, and normative strength. Preserve scoped exceptions. Example: the release handoff listed both annotated and signed tag commands, while its security note required a signed annotated tag, so use one `git tag -s` operation rather than attempting to recreate the same tag twice. Example: a planning ticket mentioned a four-event exchange including keepalives, but the merged cross-SDK PR defines the requested three-way auth handshake.
7. **Require provenance per answer.** Every answer must carry at least one stable `document_id` and full corpus `path`; use multiple sources when the primary document delegates authority or an exception changes the reading.
8. **Track uncertainty.** If sources remain ambiguous after full-document retrieval and targeted re-search, place the item in `unresolved_questions` rather than inventing a resolution.
9. **Package and index.** Validate the JSON structure, write the answer and procedure files under `/artifacts/enterprise-rag/`, index both on the task branch, and keep the branch unmerged for review.
10. **Remember only the method.** Store this procedure as playbook memory with evidence spanning several source systems; do not store the batch's answer text as reusable memory.
